sourceSnapshots.postMeasurementFormatOnlySummary: One redundant final newline removed from each SQLite/PostgreSQL 022 migration; SQL statements and business Go sources unchanged. Tested binary hashes remain the measured snapshot hashes, not the later release artifact hashes.

environment.storageIsolation: fresh SQLite directories or unique disposable PostgreSQL schemas
environment.networkScope: controlled local TCP and private-interface TCP on the same test host

methods.ordinary: Real loopback TCP HTTP, 10000 items, 200 requests per workload, concurrency 8; board is 120 cards; mixed is 40 ordinary creates plus 160 reads. Prepared data gets valid numbering outside timing.
methods.sequential: 25 real loopback TCP samples per operation and dataset size; timings include authorization and response JSON decoding. SQL budgets are counted in a separate direct handler call.
methods.status: 200 HTTP-created todo items; 200 todo-to-doing PATCH then 200 doing-to-done PATCH, concurrency 8, old then candidate adjacent for each provider.
methods.schedules: Production generation helper with controlled due time; four real HTTP readers remain active until generation completes. Control is 200 requests. No read-count cutoff during generation.
methods.events: Real HTTP event admission concurrency 8 followed by sequential production event transaction helpers; autonomous coordinator stopped to define an exact queue. Four real HTTP readers span the complete admission and processing window. Does not measure coordinator scheduling overhead.
methods.executors: Live production coordinator and four workers, normal outbound security transport wrapped only for counters, reference HTTP service and fixed Python subprocess. Twelve executions per case, 250ms command duration, production minimum 2-second receipt polling. Four HTTP readers continue to all terminal or first unknown/deadline boundary.
methods.cpu: Go test CPU includes in-process Home, local HTTP clients, and SQLite; PostgreSQL server CPU excluded. Reference server CPU and waited subprocess CPU are separate.
methods.idle: Separate native SQLite Home process, no browser or caller requests, 100Hz process CPU accounting. Zero observed ticks and IO only describe the observation window; query-free periodic behavior is separately established by no-deadline worker logic.

staticCost.inlineScope: string/slice headers and pointers included; backing data, heap objects, database caches and runtime allocations excluded

limits: Single-pass bounded measurements on a shared host; not an SLA, WAN benchmark, maximum sustainable capacity, million-user claim or long-duration soak test.
Baseline and candidate ordinary/schedule runs are not simultaneous; only added status writes were measured as adjacent old/new pairs.
Native idle observations cover SQLite Home processes only, not PostgreSQL service background activity.
Permanent numbering/planning response and struct costs, plus status-observation writes, exist even when optional automation and notifications are unused.
The 12-execution resource tests have few tail samples; preserve production polling delays instead of treating them as maximum executor capacity.
Initial filesystem-exhaustion samples are invalid and excluded; PostgreSQL normal recovery and health passed before rerun.
The PostgreSQL migration optimization changed only upgrade SQL and test preparation; completed unaffected runtime measurements were retained.
